First, we complete the square for the expression inside the square root:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-10x+24 & ={x}^{2}-2\cdot 5x+({5}^{2}-{5}^{2})+24 \\  & =({x}^{2}-2\cdot 5x+{5}^{2})-25+24 \\  & =(x-5)^{2}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
{\int }_{5+\sqrt{2}}^{7}\frac{8}{|x-5|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-10x+24}}\,\text{d}x=8{\int }_{5+\sqrt{2}}^{7}\frac{1}{|x-5|\sqrt{(x-5)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This resembles the basic integral for inverse secant:

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u=\text{arcsec}\,u+C
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u$ as the variable, we have $(x-5).$

So, let's perform the substitution

$$
u=x-5.
$$

Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Let's use the table below to change the limits from $x$ to $u.$

| $x$ | $5+\sqrt{2}$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\sqrt{2}$ | $2$ |

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{5+\sqrt{2}}^{7}\frac{8}{|x-5|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-10x+24}}\,\text{d}x & =8{\int }_{\sqrt{2}}^{2}\frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =8\,\text{arcsec}\,u\,{|}_{\sqrt{2}}^{2} \\  & =8(\text{arcsec}(2)-\text{arcsec}(\sqrt{2})) \\  & =8(\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
